title: Comments of Allegra Schecter urging FERC to choose the No Action Alternative re the Constitution Pipeline under CP13-499, et al.

documents.text:
Re: Cons tu on Pipeline Company, EA Comments
Docket numbers CP13-499-006 and CP18-5-004


Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street NE
Washington, DC 20426
September 19, 2026

Dear Secretary Reese,

I believe the Commission should choose the NO Ac on Alterna ve rather than approving the
Cons tu on Pipeline. Under the No-Ac on Alterna ve, “Cons tu on and Iroquois would not construct
any component of the Projects and, consequently, would be unable to meet the stated purpose and
need.” What is their stated purpose and need?

Cons tu on is a pipeline searching for a reason to be built. There is no purpose for it yet. It has no
customers - yet. There is no empty pipeline to which it can connect to distribute the gas to down state
New York, New England, or anywhere else. There is no public beneﬁt or convenience that is worth the
environmental risk to our water, air and land.

The Williams Company is hoping to lure an AI data center to come here to use its gas once it is built. This
area does not need, nor want our land being taken by public domain in order to support an AI Data
Center! We need to slow down the building of these Data Centers, un l Super Intelligent AI is be er
understood and controlled. The data centers themselves will consume all our water, pollute our air and
destroy our quiet, beau ful forested mountain slopes and clean freshwater streams – even more so than
the actual pipeline. This is not why people in this part of upstate New York came here to live. We enjoy
our quiet, rural communi es, our clean air and water, the ﬁsh and wildlife, just as they are.

FERC should deﬁnitely choose the NO Ac on Alterna ve!

Thank you,

Allegra Schecter
211Adair Road
Cherry Valley, NY 13320
